## Natural history notes

A large mole cricket characterized by a tan to brown cylindrical body, short wings, and broad shovel-like front legs adapted for digging through soil. In Florida, the Tawny Mole Cricket is an introduced species found in lawns, pastures, golf courses, fields, roadsides, and other grassy habitats with sandy or moist soil. It feeds heavily on grass roots and shoots while tunneling underground, sometimes becoming a serious turf and pasture pest, and males call from burrows to attract females during the breeding season.
